title: I Tested Ninja’s CrushBoss, a $230 Blender That Chops, Dices, Minces and Mixes
snippet: The food processor and blender attachments are handy, while other elements feel like overkill.
fullText:
One of the biggest roadblocks for adding countertop appliances to your kitchen is storage. For folks with a small kitchen, myself included, the struggle often looks like a constant shuffle, trading one appliance for another in the pantry. This problem is less noticeable in larger kitchens, but you might end up with more clutter than you’d like.

This modestly sized blender does far more than blend.  John Carlsen/CNET

Eventually, you need to decide if you’ll use an appliance often enough to justify getting it. In my case, I’m much more likely to choose a multipurpose product like an Instant Pot pressure cooker or an air fryer. Perhaps this is why I was excited to test out the Ninja CrushBoss, which combines a large blender, food processor and small smoothie blender into a single device. I spent the two weeks using a sample unit from Ninja in my kitchen, and I’m eager to share my thoughts. 

Four appliances in one. Well, kind of

The main appeal of the Ninja CrushBoss is that it comes with three vessels: a 72-ounce blender pitcher, a 64-ounce food processor bowl and a 26-ounce smoothie tumbler.

CrushBoss isn’t Ninja’s first attempt at an all-in-one kitchen system, as the Ninja Detect, Ninja Professional Plus and Ninja Foodi Power Blender all attempt similar feats. What sets Ninja CrushBoss apart are the PrecisionDice and MultiBlade Disc attachments for the food processor bowl, plus a better smoothie tumbler design than previous models.

			

More from CNET

Similarly, the blender’s preset programs change depending on which vessel you attach to the 1850-watt base motor, with each program running automatically to achieve the desired results. You can rotate the outer ring of the small LCD screen to choose your setting, then make the final selection by pressing the top of the screen inward to click. It’s not a touchscreen, but it’s easy enough to use once you learn the controls.

Intelligent blending features, PrepIQ and SmoothSense, track the type and consistency of what you’re blending, but I didn’t notice a difference compared to the preset programs or custom speed controls.John Carlsen/CNET

There isn’t much that’s special about the large blender pitcher, which uses largely the same design as other standalone Ninja blenders. It comes with a single blade assembly and presets for mincing, small chopping and large chopping. The smoothie tumbler is similarly simple, with its small blade assembly supporting ice crushing, blending and smoothie presets. Compared to older tumblers, the Travel Tumbler’s main upgrade is a better carrying handle, flip-top lid and a large smoothie straw — it’s more like a Stanley cup than a NutriBullet personal blender.

Last, but not least, is the food processor, which has the most accessories, including a chopping blade, dough blade, MultiBlade Disc and the PrecisionDice assembly. Where the Ninja Detect’s food processor included reversible stainless steel discs, the MultiBlade attachment is largely plastic, with specific inserts depending on the model you choose. The model I tested came with inserts for thick slices, crinkle-cut slices and shredding — Ninja also sells inserts for thin slices, french fries and julienning.

While I understand that the plastic MultiBlade Disc and inserts reduce the amount of stainless steel in the package, I can’t help but wonder about their long-term durability compared to all-metal discs.John Carlsen/CNET

I call it a kind of four-in-one appliance because the smoothie tumbler’s main benefits are, naturally, smoother blending consistency than the large pitcher and greater travel portability with the included lid and smoothie straw. You can still use the large pitcher for family-size smoothies and anything too big for the other two vessels, so adding a blending function to each vessel is largely superfluous. Similarly, the dicing kit is hardly an appliance on its own, since you’ll see it on other food processor brands like KitchenAid and Breville.

How useful is the Ninja CrushBoss?

My Ninja CrushBoss tests were informal, so I mostly wanted to see whether it could handle a few tasks, like making salads, smoothies, processing cheese and chopping a few kinds of vegetables. I tested every attachment and accessory in the box, with most receiving multiple tests.John Carlsen/CNET

Of the three vessels, I spent the most time with the food processor. I used the PrecisionDice attachment to prepare a fruit salad, which went very smoothly and had no issues with mango, watermelon, strawberries and pineapple. I pureed some blackberries with the food processor’s chopping blade to add more texture to the salad, though the smoothie attachment was ultimately a better option for crushing the blackberry seeds.

Next, I swapped the dicing attachment for the MultiBlade and sliced potatoes and cucumbers with the normal and crinkle-cut attachments. Again, the results were very good. Things were a little less consistent when I processed carrots and cabbage with the shredder for a quick coleslaw, as some bits of each remained unprocessed between the blade and lid. The amount of unprocessed vegetables was minimal, so I tossed them into a bowl of ramen instead of manually chopping them for the coleslaw.

The point of the cheese test was to find the food processor’s limits, so I’m happy to report the motor safety cutoff and error messages worked as intended when I stressed the unit too much.John Carlsen/CNET

To give the food processor a proper workout, I brought out the cheddar cheese, which I put through the shredder, slicer and dicer. As you might suspect, the cheese worked best with the shredder, with very little waste and no clogs. The other two attachments are less suitable for cheese, with the slicing disc producing passable slices. However, I clogged the dicing tool when I tried to make cheese cubes. I ultimately succeeded with some tiny cubes, but I don’t recommend it. 

	

			

	

			

									

						The Best Blenders We Tested in 2026					

							

		

While I didn’t use the dough blade attachment much, it seemed good for mixing bread dough into a state where I could knead it by hand. I ran three cycles using the dough preset — though I admit the last cycle was because I forgot to add an ingredient. One reason I finished by hand was that I could hear the motor straining a bit toward the end of the second and third cycles.

Even if I’m not 100% on board with using it for dense bread dough, the unit is plenty powerful for cookie dough and cake batter.John Carlsen/CNET

I suspect the CrushBoss can handle the job, as the manual says it can hold up to 2 pounds of dough and shut off if necessary, but it took only a minute of hand-kneading after processing to reach the consistency I wanted. My advice: Listen to your machine and avoid tasks that trigger the auto-shutoff too often. Fortunately, my testing didn’t surface any problems with the system’s durability.

Beyond the food processor bowl, little stood out about the blender pitcher and smoothie tumbler attachments. Each did well with various levels of blending, pureeing and ice crushing, but nothing so outstanding that my ancient Oster blender couldn’t also do. The biggest advantages over my modest blender are the pitcher’s size — even if it’s more than I need in my kitchen — and the tumbler’s portability. Ninja says CrushBoss isn’t suitable for hot blending, so you can’t safely use it with hot liquids.

The challenge of modular kitchen systems like Ninja CrushBoss

Somewhat paradoxically, the modular nature of the Ninja CrushBoss is also its biggest weakness — at least for me.John Carlsen/CNET

Although I’m happy that I don’t have to store three motorized bases for separate specialty appliances, all of Ninja’s vessels and attachments are bulky enough that they’d take up an entire shelf in my kitchen cabinets. There’s not really a safe way to store the extremely sharp food processor discs, so I ultimately kept them in a carrying case for a massage gun I threw out ages ago. Fortunately, you can safely store the largest blender blade assemblies in each vessel.

The other challenge is that while all of the attachments are dishwasher-safe, that only applies to the top rack. My older dishwasher’s top rack isn’t adjustable, so I can’t fit any of the vessels inside and I have to wash them all by hand. This isn’t a problem I experience with the glass jar of my Oster blender, or the slightly smaller vessel of the Tribest Backspin I tested in 2025. At least the other parts fit, which made cleanup much more manageable.

My point in calling these out isn’t to discourage anyone interested in the CrushBoss, but to note that storage space and dishwasher space still matter before you buy.

Should you buy the Ninja CrushBoss?

The CrushBoss’s value becomes more apparent as the amount of food increases.John Carlsen/CNET

As I used the Ninja CrushBoss 4-in-1, I kept coming back to one central question: “Who is this for?” Ultimately, it’s a harder question to answer than I thought. I have no problem recommending each function separately — blending, smoothies, dicing and food processing — because it seems to do all of these well enough.

For example, this particular setup should work well for two types of households: large families and meal preppers. I grew up in a large family, and having an appliance to prepare a huge amount of ingredients for every meal is a no-brainer. Another group that might benefit is the meal-prepper, regardless of household size.

Still, selling everything together in a single kit is excessive for someone like me, who has a small apartment. I have plenty of travel cups for smoothies and rarely need to process large amounts of food. Ninja thankfully offers various CrushBoss configurations and will most likely sell the attachments separately down the line, like with its older products. Personally, I’d love a configuration with only a large pitcher and food processor — I don’t need a smoothie tumbler.

At $320, the Ninja CrushBoss 4-in-1 costs about what you’d pay for separate Ninja appliances, but it is pricier than previous generations of Ninja’s modular kitchen systems, even without the dicing kit. This is a drop in the bucket compared to getting similar attachments for a Vitamix Ascent X. Despite my personal reservations, I think the Ninja CrushBoss 4-in-1 is a great idea, especially for folks looking to consolidate multiple specialty appliances into a single modular system. It taps into the reason why people love the classic KitchenAid stand mixer, and that’s a good thing.

title: AirPods just got a long-requested feature in new software update
snippet: While it was overshadowed by release of iOS 27, Apple also released a new software update for AirPods this month. The update brings a long-requested feature to supported AirPods models: custom EQ. more…
fullText:
While it was overshadowed by release of iOS 27, Apple also released a new software update for AirPods this month. The update brings a long-requested feature to supported AirPods models: custom EQ.

AirPods software details

The latest AirPods firmware build number is 9A350 for AirPods 5 and 9A348 for the other models below. The update is available for the following AirPods models:

AirPods Pro 3

AirPods 5

AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case

AirPods Pro 2 (Lightning and USB-C)

AirPods Max 2

Apple says that AirPods firmware updates are automatically installed while your AirPods are charging and within Bluetooth range of your iPhone, iPad, or Mac that’s connected to WiFi. You can check the firmware version of your AirPods in the Settings app on iPhone. 

Custom EQ comes to AirPods

Once you install the AirPods firmware update, you’ll see a long-awaited new feature in the Settings app: custom EQ.

You now have more control over how your AirPods sound thanks to the new custom EQ controls. In the Settings app, you can adjust the lows, mids, and highs of your AirPods sound.

“AirPods are designed and engineered by Apple to faithfully represent music, TV shows and movies, and calls,” Apple explains. “If you prefer a different sound profile, you can customize how AirPods represent any audio played.”

While adjusting the custom EQ settings, you can play a song from Apple Music right in the Settings app to hear the adjustments in real time.

This isn’t the most advanced equalizer feature out there. It’s a basic, three-band system. Still, it’s a long-awaited AirPods feature that Apple has finally given users—even if most will likely stick with the default levels.

You can find the new custom EQ feature in the AirPods section of the Settings app under the “Audio and Routing” menu. The feature is available on all AirPods with an H2 chip, including AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Pro 3, AirPods 4, and AirPods Max 2.

Other iOS 27 features for AirPods

Here are the other new AirPods features for iOS 27:

Settings app redesign: In iOS 27, Apple has redesigned the AirPods interface in the Settings app. The controls have been reorganized, with separate menus for Hearing Health, Find My, Live Translation, and more.

Adaptive Audio slider: In the Settings app, you now have a slider to further fine-tune Adaptive Audio mode.

GymKit: While GymKit has been around for years, it’s always required an Apple Watch. As my colleague Zac explains, iOS 27 brings the full GymKit experience to iPhone and AirPods Pro 3.

Precision Finding: You can now use Precision Finding in the Find My app on Apple Watch to locate AirPods Pro 3.

Siri AI: When paired to a compatible iPhone, AirPods can interact with Siri AI.

Wrap up

What new AirPods features are you most excited to try? Are you going to try the new custom EQ feature? Let us know down in the comments.

title: Android Auto rolls out game support, no longer in beta
snippet: Google is graduating game support on Android Auto from a limited beta to broad availability, allowing developers to bring games to your car’s display. more…
fullText:
Google is graduating game support on Android Auto from a limited beta to broad availability, allowing developers to bring games to your car’s display.

First available last year, games in Android Auto and Android Automotive bring a bit of interactive fun to the car’s display. While there’s no direct integration with things like the car’s steering wheel, it’s a nice way to add something fun to the biggest screen in your vehicle for times you might be stuck on the side of the road, waiting on an EV to charge, or other times where the vehicle is not moving.

Around 30 games are available on Android Auto today, but that list is likely to start expanding soon.

Google announced this week that game support on Android Auto is no longer in beta, meaning that game support is open to all developers rather than requiring specific approval from Google. 

	

Google says:

Bringing your game to cars lets you reach users in their vehicles during natural downtime, such as while waiting at a charging station or for a curbside order pickup. Today’s milestone means that we’re opening up access so developers can now publish games to the open testing and production tracks on Google Play. In this post, we’ll cover how to adapt your existing Android game for the car screen, focusing on key technical requirements and publishing criteria.

Android games must declare support for Android Auto and Android Automotive OS – they’re separate declarations behind the scenes, and there are many more games that support Android Automotive without Android Auto support as it stands today.

Games on Android Auto should be able to adapt to different display sizes and need to recognize when a vehicle is parked or not – games can only be played if the vehicle is parked. Games can also support controllers on Android Auto and Android Automotive. 

Google’s full documentation on what developers need to do can be found here.

title: Nothing Phone (4a) and (3a) Pro can now join Android 17 open beta
snippet: Right on schedule, Nothing is releasing Nothing OS 5.0 open beta for the Phone (4a), Phone (3a Pro, and Phone (3a) before the company’s official Android 17 release next month. more…
fullText:
Right on schedule, Nothing is releasing Nothing OS 5.0 open beta for the Phone (4a), Phone (3a Pro, and Phone (3a) before the company’s official Android 17 release next month.

The Android 17 package contains a few changes for Nothing phones. It was first released as a beta update for the Nothing Phone (3) with visual changes to the system UI and animations across the board. The update also includes new widgets, updates to the camera app, and a dedicated Glyph app for light controls and features.

You can check out the full changelog in our previous coverage. At its core, it brings Nothing’s devices up to date with the latest version of Android. Of course, this company is known for creating its own spin on both hardware and software.

Right now, though, Nothing is actively rolling out Android 17 beta access to the Nothing Phone (4a), Phone (3a) Pro, and Phone (3a). The update leaves out the Phone (3a) Lite, which is expected to get access later in the year. Users with either of those devices should now be able to access the Nothing OS 5.0 open beta, which puts it on par with the Phone (3).

	

In terms of scheduling, Nothing is right on time. The company posted its release schedule when the first open beta rolled out, and it remains unchanged. The three devices announced today will be followed by the Phone (2a) and Phone (2a) Plus in October.

The same post also notes the Phone (4a) and Phone (3a) series will be pushed to the official Android 17 build in early November. The rollout is expected to end sometime in January 2027.

For the time being, Phone (4a) and (3a) series users should now be able to access Nothing OS 5.0 in its early stages.

title: Samsung has delayed its Android 17 update
snippet: Samsung appears to be delaying the rollout of its Android 17 update, at least slightly, with pushback in some regions. more…
fullText:
Samsung appears to be delaying the rollout of its Android 17 update, at least slightly, with pushback in some regions.

The launch of a stable One UI 9 rollout for Galaxy S26 was first announced last week, with the Android 17-based update landing first on Samsung’s current flagship before expanding to more devices. Samsung explicitly said the rollout was supposed to start on September 16, but it doesn’t appear to have shown up for anyone just yet. 

While the reason is unclear, SammyGuru spotted a sort of confirmation that Samsung has delayed its Android 17 in some capacity.

A press release around the One UI 9 rollout on Samsung’s Newsroom in Thailand noted a rollout date of September 21 originally, but was updated to say September 28, and now appears to have been updated again to remove a specific date altogether, only saying “September 2026” at this point.

	

This isn’t unprecedented; Samsung has had numerous major updates be delayed quietly at the last moment, but it’s certainly not the best start for One UI 9’s rollout. Hopefully, whatever issues are pushing Samsung’s schedule back can be fixed as soon as possible.

title: Adobe Premiere for Android launches for free with layered video editing, YouTube templates
snippet: Months after it arrived on iPhone, Adobe Premiere’s mobile version is now available on Android devices with layered video editing, templates, foldable optimization, and more. more…
fullText:
Months after it arrived on iPhone, Adobe Premiere’s mobile version is now available on Android devices with layered video editing, templates, foldable optimization, and more.

Adobe Premiere Pro is widely recognized as a powerful video editing suite on desktop machines, but Adobe’s last version for mobile devices vanished a while back. Now, Adobe Premiere is once again available on Android, delivering what appears to be a very capable video editor that promises to be a solution across all Android devices.

This is the same app that debuted on iPhone in late 2025, and it brings quite a few features with it.

Some of the key features include:

	

Enhance Audio: Reduce background noise, clean up voiceovers, etc

Multi-track timeline: Manage multiple videos, sound effects, music, etc

Templates: Custom-made templates to speed up editing

Effects: Transitions, creative assets, Adobe Stock integration

Export: Up to 4K editing + export

The app already has wide support of different Android devices and form factors, including optimization for foldable smartphones. There’s also a built-in voice recorder.

Adobe says that more features are coming, including support for Adobe Fonts in creating text overlays, the ability to transfer projects to Premiere Pro on desktop, “beat detection,” cropping, and more. 

The big deal here, though, is that Adobe Premiere for Android is free. You don’t need a Creative Cloud subscription, you don’t need to sit through ads, and there are no watermarks either. Adobe says you can purchase upgrades for “additional generative credits and storage,” but that’s optional.

Requirements for Adobe Premiere on Android include 5GB of RAM or more and Android 13 or newer.

Lovable has crossed annual run-rate revenue of $600 million, the company’s co-founder Fabian Hedin said at the HumanX summit in Amsterdam on Thursday. The vibe-coding platform in June said that number was around $500 million.

Hedin said the startup has focused on growing its enterprise business, and claimed that people at two-thirds of Fortune 500 companies are now using its product. Its customers include Microsoft, Nvidia, and Deutsche Telekom.

“You can use these tools [like Codex or Claude code] to output code. The difference is that Lovable does not output code. The output is a product, and increasingly so, a business. The company has raised over $700 million in two rounds just eight months apart. Last December, it raised $300 million from Menlo Ventures and CapitalG at a $6.6 billion valuation. title: Trove of Stolen Sensitive FBI Employee Data Is Significant Intelligence Risk
snippet: ShinyHunters has previously extorted companies and schools, but the sensitivity of this data makes this breach different.
fullText:
Hackers from the group ShinyHunters claim to have stolen personal data of “all” FBI employees and applicants, according to a report published Tuesday by 404 Media.

The group, which was also behind a breach that disrupted software used by 9,000 schools during final exams in May, reportedly gained access to the FBI’s recruitment site via an exploit in Oracle’s PeopleSoft product. ShinyHunters says it now has sensitive data on individuals who applied for FBI jobs as well as current employees, according to 404 Media. ShinyHunters couldn’t be reached for comment.

As of Wednesday afternoon, the apply.fbijobs.gov site shows a maintenance page reading, “We’re sniffing out site updates for you!” The main FBI Jobs home page serves up a “503 Service Temporarily Unavailable” error page. The bureau’s page highlighting eligibility for new applicants is live with a “System Unavailable” banner reading, “Apply.fbijobs.gov and the Special Agent Application Portal are currently unavailable.”

			

More from CNET

The FBI’s jobs website shows a maintenance page following a breach by hackers who claim to have stolen sensitive personnel records.Screenshot by Jeff Carlson/CNET

“The FBI is aware of a cyber-criminal enterprise group claiming a compromise of the FBIJobs.gov portal and alleged impact to FBI employee personally identifiable information,” a spokesperson for the FBI told CNET via email. “While the point of breach is still undetermined — whether a third-party or the FBI’s enterprise — we are actively and aggressively investigating this matter and working closely with those third-party providers that support FBIJobs.gov to mitigate any and all risk.”

ShinyHunters has been linked to numerous ransomware attacks, including a breach of 4.4 million TransUnion credit records and access to servers belonging to Rockstar Games, the developer of the Grand Theft Auto series. The group usually demands extortion payments to prevent it from leaking the stolen information.

However, the attack on the FBI’s data is different and has potentially much more serious implications.

The group reportedly wants the FBI to correct what it calls false allegations in a Public Service Announcement that the FBI issued about it. The report notes that ShinyHunter “actors commonly use harassment strategies, sending threatening text messages and phone calls to victims and their family members, and in some cases swatting.”

In an email to The New York Times, a representative of ShinyHunters wrote, “We reiterate we are not extorting the FBI and this is not financially motivated… Our intention, goal and motive is to solely set the record straight.”

But the nature of the stolen data elevates this breach beyond corporate extortion.

Joseph Cox, who broke the story at 404 Media, wrote via email, “This data presents significant national security and counterintelligence risks, and isn’t in the hands of a foreign intelligence agency, but a group of likely younger, English-speaking hackers.”

A security analyst who asked to remain anonymous to avoid retaliation from the hacking group reiterated that this is a serious national security issue. “Remember, the FBI is tasked with both counterespionage and counterterrorism,” they said. “This could destroy [FBI employees’ ability] to go undercover, travel to other countries and more,” including threats to individuals and families.

Asked about the group’s claim that it has nothing to do with extortion, the analyst said, “Never trust anything they say. Ever.” 

They said that advice also comes directly from colleagues who advise companies on how to handle the extortions. Gaining access to such sensitive data could be monetarily valuable to a state-level intelligence agency.

The FBI has seen other notable cyberattacks this year, including “suspicious activities” on the system the bureau uses to manage wiretapping and surveillance and claims by an Iran-backed group said to breach the personal email of FBI Director Kash Patel.

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Jeff Carlson
						

						

							Senior Writer						
					

											

								

											Jeff Carlson writes about mobile technology at CNET, from cellular phone plans to devices and emerging technology.
															
						See full bio

title: Pixel 11 starts testing ‘Call for Me’ to have Gemini phone on your behalf
snippet: Following Direct My Call and Hold for Me, Google is introducing “Call for Me” on the Pixel 11 series. more…
fullText:
Following Direct My Call and Hold for Me, Google is introducing “Call for Me” on the Pixel 11 series.

Reminiscent of Google Duplex, this Gemini Intelligence feature is officially an “early experiment” to let Google handle “routine phone calls” to book appointments, place items on hold, and reschedule reservations. Examples include 

reserve patio seating at a restaurant

check if a hardware store has a specific part in stock

move your haircut appointment to next Thursday

Google says it will “respect the time of the neighborhood shops and front-desk staff answering the phone,” and that “calls made by Gemini on behalf of the user represent real customers conducting real transactions.”

Asking AI to speak on your behalf is a big step that requires genuine trust. That’s why we built this experience around user control.

Your Pixel 11 will “call on your behalf using the Gemini app.” Users see a live transcript and can take over at any point.  Gemini will “introduce itself” and “handle the conversation with the person on the other end.” As part of this, it can wait on hold and navigate any automated phone menus.

	

Google is “starting small to get the experience right.” As of today, an early preview is rolling out to Gemini subscribers using the enrolled in the Phone by Google beta on the Pixel 11, 11 Pro, 11 Pro XL, and 11 Pro Fold in the US. More details are available here.

title: Android’s Digital Wellbeing appears to be ditching ‘Heads up’ walking alerts
snippet: Google appears to be pulling the plug on a Digital Wellbeing feature called “Heads up” which is designed to help you stay off of your phone for extended periods of time while walking. more…
fullText:
Google appears to be pulling the plug on a Digital Wellbeing feature called “Heads up” which is designed to help you stay off of your phone for extended periods of time while walking.

Introduced in 2021, “Heads up” was designed to help you curb your smartphone use while walking since, when looking at your phone, you’re probably not fully aware of your surroundings. Alerts such as “Look ahead” and “Watch your step” would appear if you were using your phone while walking for a certain length of time.

Now, Google seems to be removing it.

In the Digital Wellbeing v1.48.975819457.beta release, the folks over at Android Authority noticed strings regarding “Heads up deprecation.” Google explicitly says:

	

Walking detection is going away soon

There’s no word on why it’s being removed, though it’s certainly odd given that the feature at least appears to run on device. It’s easy to guess that the feature was probably underused, being an opt-in feature, but it’s strange seeing as there’s no obvious burden to just leaving it in place. 

As it stands, the feature is still active and, with the altered strings only in the beta track, it’s probably not going away imminently, but we’ll have to wait and see what other details come to light as the removal nears.

title: Tim Cook meets EU chief Ursula von der Leyen as bloc pushes new child safety rules
snippet: Keeping with Apple’s pledge that Tim Cook would remain involved in Apple’s government relations around the world after stepping down as CEO, he met this week with Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Keeping with Apple’s pledge that Tim Cook would remain involved in Apple’s government relations around the world after stepping down as CEO, he met this week with Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission. Here are the details.

Tim Cook discusses EU Kids Act with EC President

When Apple announced that Tim Cook would step down as CEO on September 1, the company said:

As executive chairman, Cook will assist with certain aspects of the company, including engaging with policymakers around the world.

Since taking up the job of executive chairman, Cook has kept with this promise.

Just days ago, Bloomberg reported that Cook would attend a White House state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping, which is scheduled for Thursday evening, September 24.

The report came just a few days before Cook posted on X that he had welcomed Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese at Apple Park.

It was great to welcome @AlboMP to Apple Park this morning to talk about the incredible work of our teams and our longstanding commitment to Australia. I was grateful to share some of our newest innovations, including strong and intuitive controls to help keep kids safe online. pic.twitter.com/EQKmIkP3uC

— Tim Cook (@tim_cook) September 19, 2026

After the meeting, Albanese reportedly shared that Cook described Australia’s social media restrictions for children as “world-leading.”

Yesterday, Cook continued his string of encounters with world leaders, sitting down with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen.

In a post on X, von der Leyen said the two discussed the EU Kids Act and “agreed on the importance of privacy, safety and security for children.”

Good discussion with @tim_cook in the margins of UNGA.

 We discussed the EU Kids Act, and agreed on the importance of privacy, safety and security for children.

title: Microsoft’s New Surface Laptops Embody the PC-Phone Marriage Snapdragon Promised Years Ago
snippet: Qualcomm’s PC chips were developed with the company’s phone DNA. Two generations in, we’re seeing payoffs.
fullText:
On the stage for the second day of keynotes at Snapdragon Summit 2026, Microsoft Corporate VP of Surface Devices Brett Ostrum revealed new versions of the company’s 12-inch Surface Pro and 13-inch Surface laptops, both of which now run Qualcomm’s Snapdragon Elite X2 chips for improved performance and battery life. These chips had come to larger Surface devices earlier in the year, and arrived in the smaller sizes of Microsoft’s portable PC lineup.

Along with the chip upgrade, both of the updated Surface devices have increased RAM options of 16GB and 24GB (up from 8GB and 16GB in their predecessors).

But some hidden advantages of running Qualcomm’s Snapdragon Elite X2, which was introduced at last year’s Snapdragon Summit, are downstream of the years the company spent developing smartphone silicon. 

			

More from CNET

The first Snapdragon X Elite chips were revealed in 2023 as Qualcomm’s big return to PC silicon, attempting to outdo Apple laptops in battery life and performance. A big part of the company’s pitch was using what it learned making phone chips to see benefits in the laptop space. Now, we’re seeing evidence of that DNA paying off.

For instance, Ostrum told me after the keynote that the new Surface devices have superior cameras to their rivals thanks to the image signal processing on the Elite X2 chips, inherited from phone camera hardware, that will make you look amazing on Zoom calls.

The 13-inch Surface Laptop and 12-inch Surface Pro received Snapdragon X2 upgrades, and the new Surface Mouse has haptics to buzz and pulse your palm.Katie Collins/CNET

Before, Apple had taken the crown of image quality in its laptop webcams, Ostrum said. But thanks to Qualcomm’s investment in ISP and the camera pipeline, the Surface devices have seen a big turnaround in the video quality captured by their webcams. 

“With our [Surface] Pro and laptops that we announced earlier this year [with] Snapdragon X2 Elite, we took the No. 1 and No. 2 spots from Apple in terms of camera quality,” Ostrum said, referring to DxOMark’s laptop rankings. Those rankings currently place Microsoft’s 13.8-inch Surface Laptop and 13-inch Surface Pro in first and second place, above Apple’s MacBook Pro models, in camera quality.

It’s not the first thing consumers or commercial buyers look at when shopping for laptops and two-in-ones, but people now spend so much time in Teams and Zoom meetings that camera quality is more important than consumers might admit. And considering how much the bar has been raised by ever-improving phone cameras, it’s no surprise that people want and expect an improved webcam.

“You want to look good when you show up [on camera], and it’s important to us, it’s important to our customers. And so it’s a fairly straightforward approach for us to say we want to make this look as good as we can,” Ostrum said.

We’re not just talking about better camera hardware, either. Ostrum was quick to say that it isn’t the lenses or sensors that make the difference — it’s the image processing pipeline Qualcomm has refined.

“I can put the same sensors into multiple silicon platforms, but the best solution is going to come with a Qualcomm ISP,” Ostrum said. “If you compare an Intel-based one of our commercial devices to a Qualcomm-based solution, you will see the difference.”

Both the new 12-inch Surface Pro (left) and 13-inch Surface Laptop (right) pack Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X2 Elite chips.David Lumb/CNET

Phone chip DNA doesn’t just help with cameras — it boosts battery, too

That’s not the end of smartphones’ influence on laptops. The older x86 chips may have been adapted to laptops, but they originated in a world where PCs plugged into walls, Ostrum said, implying that they struggled with battery life. But the Snapdragon phone chip DNA and its emphasis on performance per watt have noticeably extended the battery life on Surface devices while also delivering the fast speeds consumers need for their tasks. 

“People raved about the first generation of devices from a performance perspective, but the thing that we heard unanimously that was just a huge delight was, ‘The battery life’s incredible. The battery life’s incredible. The battery life’s incredible,'” Ostrum said. 

There’s more that goes into the battery life of the Surface Pro and Surface laptop than the chip, including redesigning the interior for better thermal management. Roughly speaking, better heat management means more time running at high performance and less energy spent cooling the device down, which means more battery life. It’s all connected.

“We oftentimes will see as much gen-over-gen performance improvement from the thermal design that we iterate on as we do from the chip improvement gen-over-gen,” Ostrum said. 

Still, that’s combining what Microsoft does best with the advantages of Qualcomm silicon, at least as far as Ostrum sees it. Microsoft expects 22.5 hours of battery life from the second-gen 13-inch Surface laptop, which is slightly down from the 24 hours offered by its predecessor. We’ll see how those expectations bear out in our testing. 

What is true is how much longer those expectations are than what they were before Microsoft switched to Qualcomm — the Surface Laptop 5 and 6 with Intel-based chips had 18.5 hours of expected battery life, though the internet is strewn with reports of units only lasting half that time, or even less. Switching to a chip that inherited priorities and design architecture from mobile silicon seems to have helped.

Editors’ note: David Lumb’s travel costs were covered by Qualcomm. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

title: Brazil court tells Apple to add age checks for casino app purchases
snippet: A Brazilian court has ordered Apple to tighten age controls around a casino-style app on the App Store, including requiring age verification before making in-app purchases. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
A Brazilian court has ordered Apple to tighten age controls around a casino-style app on the App Store, including requiring age verification before making in-app purchases. Here are the details.

Apple ordered to strengthen App Store age checks in Brazil

As reported by Tilt, São Paulo’s Court of Justice has granted an emergency injunction requiring Apple to restrict minors’ access to the “Casino Roulette: Roulettist” app.

The decision came after four child and adolescent rights groups filed a civil lawsuit in July, alleging that minors were able to download casino-style games from the App Store and purchase virtual chips with real money, despite Casino Roulette: Roulettist carrying an 18+ age rating.

In the decision, the court gave Apple five days to block new downloads of Casino Roulette: Roulettist by users registered as minors, and require “age verification for purchases of virtual chips with real money to continue playing or expand the in-app experience,” says Tilt.

Beyond the specific app, the decision also bars Apple from allowing new apps with equivalent casino-style mechanics onto the App Store without effective age controls.

Tilt says the court also told Apple to preserve all records related to the app and present a technical report detailing the measures it has taken. The court also established a daily fine of R$100,000 (roughly $19,500) for noncompliance.

Tilt reached out to Apple for comment, but the company had not responded at the time of publication.

title: Apple challenges OpenAI’s forensic analysis in trade secrets case, seeks access to hardware R&D
snippet: Apple has asked the court overseeing its lawsuit against OpenAI and other defendants to let its own experts review forensic images used in the case, while also seeking documents related to parts of OpenAI’s hardware R&D. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple has asked the court overseeing its lawsuit against OpenAI and other defendants to let its own experts review forensic images used in the case, while also seeking documents related to parts of OpenAI’s hardware R&D. Here are the details.

A bit of background

In early July, Apple sued former employees, OpenAI, and io Products, accusing them of trade secret misappropriation.

The lawsuit involves former Apple employees who allegedly took confidential information with them when they left the company. Apple also alleges that former employee Chang Liu coached another Apple employee on materials to review ahead of an OpenAI interview, while Tang Tan directed Apple job candidates to bring hardware components and other materials to interviews.

More recently, Apple said an initial forensic inspection of a MacBook used by Liu after leaving the company showed that he had used a confidential Apple circuit schematic to run a simulation while working at OpenAI. Apple also said the MacBook pointed to Liu’s use of a Mac mini, which the company has since sought access to as part of the case.

OpenAI has since refuted Apple’s allegations, arguing that this situation is “a mess of Apple’s own making,” since the company’s allegedly lax offboarding and security practices made it easier for employees to unintentionally retain access to confidential information after leaving.

One of the many points of contention in the case is Apple’s request for expedited discovery, which OpenAI has opposed. Another is Apple’s request for a preliminary injunction that would restrict OpenAI’s use of Apple’s alleged trade secrets while the lawsuit proceeds, potentially affecting its ongoing hardware development.

Apple argues that it needs expedited access to certain evidence precisely because OpenAI is still developing its hardware product, meaning that any alleged use of Apple’s trade secrets could become further intertwined with that work and increasingly difficult to undo.

OpenAI, in turn, argues that Apple has not shown why a separate expedited discovery process is warranted, and says that Apple’s requests are too broad.

Due to this impasse, the court asked both sides to submit a joint filing laying out their respective positions on expedited discovery. That document, filed last Friday, has now been made public.

Apple wants access to forensic images, R&D material

In the joint filing, Apple asks the court to allow its own forensic experts to review the underlying forensic images that the defendants’ experts relied on to analyze Liu’s devices and determine whether he accessed or used Apple’s confidential information after leaving the company.

Apple says one of its forensic experts has already identified what it describes as “critical flaws” in that analysis, and argues that its experts need direct access to determine whether there were other problems with the defendants’ forensic analysis.

Here’s Apple:

Apple’s forensic expert has already uncovered several critical flaws in the analysis conducted by Defendants’ experts, including (1) failures to locate files on Mr. Liu’s Mac Mini that were demonstrably used and stored on that device and (2) incorrect conclusions that the presence of files with zero bytes or an empty kMDItemLastUsedDate field on the Mac Mini means those files were not accessed. […] Giving Apple’s experts direct access to these forensic images is critical to understanding what other errors Defendants’ experts may have committed.

OpenAI argues that Apple’s experts should not be given unrestricted access to the forensic images, proposing instead that a neutral forensic expert handle them under a jointly agreed protocol.

Apple argues that this would put it at a disadvantage, since the defendants’ own forensic experts have already had direct access to the same material.

In addition to the forensic material, Apple is seeking expedited access to documents related to OpenAI’s hardware development, including work on metal finishes, power management, and battery functionality.

OpenAI previously argued that its metal finishes were developed independently, without using Apple confidential information, and that a simulation Liu ran using an Apple confidential file had nothing to do with its upcoming product.

Apple is now asking for the underlying development records so it can test those claims, which OpenAI says is just an attempt to “snoop on a competitor.”

Here’s Apple:

As Defendants have now put their development at issue, they must prove their assertions that they “developed their own standard metal finishes and colors” by producing supporting documents. Apple is not requesting “a complete technical record of OpenAI’s development of any technology,” as OpenAI asserts, but rather technology related to “metal finishes, power management, or battery functionality,” the technology that Defendants have put at issue in defending against Apple’s claims.

And here’s OpenAI:

This demand for a complete technical record of OpenAI’s development of any technology within Apple’s broad categories is overbroad and premature, and an apparent attempt to snoop on a competitor. Apple’s request is not even limited to OpenAI’s first product under development, which Apple expressed ostensible concern about […]—it encompasses any research and development. And it requires OpenAI to reveal its trade secrets before Apple has revealed its own (which are the subject of this lawsuit)—placing this request far beyond the scope of merits-based discovery, let alone “expedited” discovery.

The joint filing also touches on several other points of contention, including:

Apple’s broader request for forensic images from devices used by Liu, Tan, former Apple employee Yu-Ting “Alyssa” Peng, and another OpenAI employee that contain or previously contained what Apple defines as “Apple Originated Information;

Records related to Liu’s use of AI tools, after the defendants said a forensic investigation found no evidence that he used an Apple confidential file with platforms including ChatGPT, Codex, Claude, or OpenClaw;

Interview-related documents from OpenAI’s Consumer Hardware Products Group, including materials showing what the group actually uses during interviews and communications with departing Apple employees;

Interrogatories that OpenAI says could reach more than 400 former Apple employees now working at the company.

Apple is also seeking the full LINE conversations between Liu and Peng, which include exchanges in which Peng asked Liu technical questions about Apple work after he had left the company.

The defendants had already submitted excerpts from those conversations in opposing Apple’s request for a preliminary injunction, but Apple argues that it should be allowed to review the full exchanges rather than only the messages the defendants chose to submit.

title: iOS 27 adds convenient new iPhone feature you’ll use all the time
snippet: iOS 27 has arrived, with Siri AI and new Apple Intelligence features as big highlights. But one of my favorite features is a convenient addition for quickly pasting items from your iPhone’s clipboard. Here’s how it works. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 has arrived, with Siri AI and new Apple Intelligence features as big highlights. But one of my favorite features is a convenient addition for quickly pasting items from your iPhone’s clipboard. Here’s how it works.

iOS 27 adds paste shortcut above keyboard for one-tap access to your clipboard

Every year Apple adds a bunch of new features to iOS, and this year that includes upgrades to Apple Wallet, Messages, CarPlay, and more.

Many new features might go easily overlooked by the average iPhone user.

But there’s one iOS 27 addition in particular that I suspect readers will find themselves using a lot.

After you copy text to your iPhone’s clipboard, or a link or photo, iOS 27 adds a paste shortcut above the keyboard when you open a new text field.

The idea is simple: if you copy something, then immediately switch to another app, or open some other text field, Apple knows there’s a very good chance you want to paste there.

So rather than requiring you to open the copy/paste menu and hit paste from there, the paste suggestion appears automatically above the keyboard—offering one-tap convenience.

You’ll even see a preview of what’s on the clipboard, right there in the top keyboard row. So if it’s text, you’ll know what that text is, and if it’s an image you’ll see a small thumbnail preview.

It’s the kind of feature that I never would have thought to ask for, but in using the iOS 27 beta over the summer it quickly proved very convenient in everyday use.

title: iPhone 18 Pro one week later: Zero compromises
snippet: I’ve been using iPhone 18 Pro for the past week after a full year as an iPhone Air user. And while there are advantages with each model, my main takeaway about iPhone 18 Pro so far is that it has zero compromises. Here’s what I mean. more…
fullText:
I’ve been using iPhone 18 Pro for the past week after a full year as an iPhone Air user. And while there are advantages with each model, my main takeaway about iPhone 18 Pro so far is that it has zero compromises. Here’s what I mean.

iPhone 18 Pro: The best camera system, battery life, and performance

If you want to buy a new iPhone, chances are the iPhone 18 Pro is a strong contender.

I’ve had mine for a week now, a Burgundy model that replaced my iPhone Air. And despite loving the Air a lot, it’s hard to match Apple’s no-compromise approach to the iPhone 18 Pro.

Cameras are better and far more versatile on iPhone 18 Pro compared to the Air. Telephoto and Ultra Wide lenses are great for specific use cases, but even the Main camera is better on iPhone 18 Pro.

Battery life is similarly impressive. I generally found the iPhone Air’s battery good enough for everyday use, and only needed to charge mid-day occasionally. But with iPhone 18 Pro I don’t even have to think about battery.

Performance is fantastic too. The A20 Pro chip makes everything on the iPhone feel fast, and I’ve even noticed a more responsive Siri AI. Thanks to the vapor chamber, I haven’t had any issues of overheating either, which the Air sometimes struggled with.

I’m not a pro photographer, and if you want battery tests or performance benchmarks, my colleague Chance’s iPhone 18 Pro review has you covered. But after a week with iPhone 18 Pro, that word “best” keeps coming back to me.

iPhone 18 Pro (and Pro Max) pack the absolute best camera system Apple makes, have the best battery life, and perform better than any other models. I’ve even noticed smaller improvements: the better built-in speakers and Dynamic Island upgrades are highlights.

There are measurable differences in all these areas, but I also appreciate just knowing my iPhone has the “best” Apple offers in key areas that matter most. There’s no wondering: would these pictures of my family look better if I used a different iPhone? Would this slowdown have happened?

All the positives of iPhone 18 Pro aside though, I’ll admit that I’m still very intrigued by the forthcoming iPhone Duo.

iPhone Duo, like iPhone Air, will be compromised but so compelling

The iPhone Air and iPhone Duo share a lot in common. Besides having similar design traits, they also both have shortcomings.

Like my iPhone Air, the iPhone Duo will have a worse camera system than iPhone 18 Pro. Battery might be comparable but definitely worse than the Pro Max, and I suspect sustained performance will lag a bit too. iPhone Duo will also lack Face ID and the Action button.

Yet despite these compromises, I’m very excited to get my hands on the device. 

That’s because it offers a lot of compelling innovations not found in iPhone 18 Pro. The foldable form factor represents arguably the biggest iPhone hardware change ever.

I’ve been enjoying my iPhone 18 Pro a lot. But guess what happened when I picked up the iPhone Air the other day?

I instantly said, “Wow.”

Here’s my iPhone 18 Pro Max review:

Do not buy an iPhone Air unless you want to immediately return every other phone forever.

— Ben Thompson (@benthompson) September 21, 2026

The Air’s thinness had become the norm for me after a year of use. But several days into using iPhone 18 Pro, I was able to find fresh appreciation for how futuristic the Air feels. And I suspect iPhone Duo will evoke similar feelings—not just for its design, but its utility too.

I’m excited to have an iPad-like experience with the iPhone that fits in my pocket. That’s true despite being admittedly torn about the downsides the Duo will bring.

The days of Apple offering a single “best” iPhone are gone. If you want a model with zero compromises, iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max seem fantastic. But for something more futuristic and unique, I still can’t wait to try iPhone Duo.

title: Google says Gemini 4 release is coming ‘as soon as possible’
snippet: As its rivals continue to iterate quickly, Google has confirmed that its Gemini 4 flagship AI model is nearing release and that it is coming “as soon as possible.” more…
fullText:
As its rivals continue to iterate quickly, Google has confirmed that its Gemini 4 flagship AI model is nearing release and that it is coming “as soon as possible.”

Google DeepMind chief Koray Kavukcuoglu confirmed to The Information at the publication’s AI Agenda Live Summit this week that its next flagship Gemini model, Gemini 4, has entered “post-training,” a phase in which the model’s behavior is refined ahead of a public release. This includes safety testing and implementing guardrails, with internal testing underway using Gemini 4 to power Antigravity.

In other words, Google is getting closer to the release of Gemini 4.

Kavukcuoglu explained:

	

Our intention is to, like—as soon as possible—to release an early post-training output because we see the results and we are excited… [to] continue the fast-paced iterations.

He adds that he hopes the model will be released “much earlier” than the end of 2026, but a specific timeline was not shared.

The update comes just days after Anthropic and OpenAI have both launched major updates to their respective flagship AI models in recent weeks. Responding to the idea that Google has “fallen behind,” Kavukcuoglu said that “I have the utmost trust in the team” and that “in my mind, it’s a certainty that we are always gonna be at the frontier.”

Google’s last major flagship model release was in November 2025 with Gemini 3 Pro, followed by Gemini 3.1 Pro in February 2026. There have been several updates to Flash and other models in the time since, most recently with Gemini 3.8 Flash. Google teased Gemini 3.5 Pro over the Summer, but never ended up releasing the model, and this week’s conversation with The Information sheds no light on whether or not that model will be released – Kavukcuoglu said that Google “took a little bit of a step back” to focus on its Flash models instead, but that the current focus is on releasing Gemini 4.

Speaking on AGI, a common conversation around other major AI model updates, Kavukcuoglu says that “the conversation is more about are we able to build intelligent agents that we can trust.”

title: Online CVS Shoppers Might Be Able to Cash In on a $20.5 Million Settlement
snippet: The pharmacy chain denies wrongdoing, but is settling anyway.
fullText:
Popular pharmacy chain CVS has been hit with a lawsuit that alleges the company sold data from customers who shopped on its websites (cvs.com and cvshealth.com) or the mobile app. 

The lawsuit alleges that CVS disclosed private health information, browsing data and more from users to advertising company Criteo and other third parties, though the pharmacy denies any wrongdoing. It has settled to the tune of $20.5 million to avoid additional expenses by continuing the lawsuit and other business disruptions. 

Email notifications (PDF) for potential class members were sent out earlier in September, but the deadline to submit the claim form is Nov. 16, 2026. If you’ve ever shopped on any of the CVS websites or mobile apps prior to July 27, 2026, you’re considered eligible to receive payment, but you must still submit a claim. 

			

More from CNET

According to the official settlement website, customers who submit a claim without documentation may receive up to $5, and those who submit a claim with valid documentation of belonging to the class may receive up to $10, but the amount may be reduced depending on the number of valid claims submitted. 

As is typical with class action lawsuits, potential class members may also opt out of the settlement. Opting out of the settlement will prevent payment, but will allow you to maintain your rights to directly sue the company yourself. The final date to opt out of the settlement is Nov. 1, 2026.

The final hearing is set to take place on Dec. 1, 2026, and if the court approves the settlement, payments will be issued 120 days after approval. Class members can be paid via check, PayPal, Venmo or Zelle.

title: I’m Enamored With the Xiaomi 18 Pro Max’s Rear Second Screen
snippet: With freshly unveiled Snapdragon 8 Elite chips, Xiaomi’s 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max represent a new generation of Android flagship devices.
fullText:
Chinese tech giant Xiaomi is officially the first phone-maker to use Qualcomm’s freshly unveiled premium chipsets in its new flagship phones. The Xiaomi 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max were announced on Wednesday in Beijing and are powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, respectively, making them two of the most powerful smartphones on the market right now.

But that market is initially limited to China, although a global launch for the phones will take place before the end of 2026. Like other Xiaomi phones, they won’t be coming to the US.

I went hands-on with the phones at the Snapdragon Summit in Hawaii, where Qualcomm had lifted the lid on the new chips just 24 hours earlier. The two models look almost identical aside from size and bear more than a passing resemblance to the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max, which are also new this month.

			

More from CNET

The Xiaomi 18 Pro Max is the first phone to use Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chip.Katie Collins/CNET

One major difference is the rear OLED screen, which sits beside the camera module (and was also on the 17 Pro series). Xiaomi says this display can show important notifications when your phone is face down on the table — a little like Nothing’s light-up glyph system — allowing you to mindfully disengage from scrolling without completely cutting yourself off. For this particular use case, I think Nothing might have the edge, as less time looking at screens is probably better for us. But I enjoyed the widgets and animated wallpapers, as well as the upgraded selfie-shooting experience the display unlocks.

Even though front-facing cameras have improved dramatically in recent years, photo quality can never quite compare with the pictures rear cameras deliver. But the second screen lets you use the rear camera for selfies and vlogging, just as you might use the front camera on your phone.

I’m a longtime fan of Xiaomi’s cameras, and while I haven’t had a chance to fully test the 18 Pro Max, the company’s previous phones and continued partnership with Leica give me every reason to hope this new generation will continue to deliver. The 18 Pro Max has a 200-megapixel main camera, a 200-megapixel telephoto camera that supports macro photography as close as 12 centimeters (4.72 inches), and a 50-megapixel ultrawide camera. In my brief hands-on time with the phone, I was pleased with the quality of the selfies I snapped — they’d have been straight to Instagram if it had been my own phone.

I was pleased with the selfie photo quality.Katie Collins/CNET

Privacy Display

Another standout feature of the 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max is the Privacy Display, which works similarly to Samsung’s technology of the same name on the Galaxy S26 Ultra. Privacy Display restricts viewing angles so you can see only the screen when you’re looking at it straight on.

With Xiaomi’s version, you can choose whether to apply the tech to the full screen, individual apps or split screen, so that it blocks only the top or bottom. I tried this out with Privacy Display applied to the gallery at the top half of the screen. I could still make out the general shapes on the display, but it did obscure and darken the details, so I couldn’t see the content of the photos when I turned the phone to the side.

The 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max that I saw were both China editions featuring 7,000-mAh and 8,500-mAh silicon-carbon batteries, respectively. The versions that eventually go on sale in Europe and other regions may have different specs, but we won’t have long to wait to find out, with the global launch coming within the next few months.

Editor’s note: Katie Collins’ travel costs for the Snapdragon Summit were covered by Qualcomm. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

title: Samsung’s battery upgrades for Galaxy S27 Ultra and Pro leak – is it enough?
snippet: A new leak reveals the battery sizes of Samsung’s upcoming Galaxy S27 Ultra and S27 Pro including some long overdue upgrades, but do you think it’s enough? more…
fullText:
A new leak reveals the battery sizes of Samsung’s upcoming Galaxy S27 Ultra and S27 Pro including some long overdue upgrades, but do you think it’s enough?

Following Samsung’s adoption of silicon-carbon battery tech on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 series, it was inevitable that the Galaxy S27 series would jump on board. That’s not directly confirmed yet, but a regulatory leak (via GSMArena) offers a look at the rated capacities of Samsung’s new flagships.

These are rated capacities, with advertised capacity generally being a bit higher. As a comparison, the Galaxy S26 Ultra has an advertised battery capacity of 4,855 mAh, but an advertised capacity of 5,000 mAh. So, with that in mind:

Galaxy S27 Ultra: Rated 5,534 mAh | Advertised likely 5,700~ mAh 

Galaxy S27 Pro: Rated 5,087 mAh | Advertised likely 5,200~ mAh 

There’s no direct comparison for the Pro model, but the Galaxy S26 sits at 4,300 mAh at around the same physical size, so this is a huge jump. 

	

For Samsung’s full-size flagship, the Galaxy S27 Ultra is looking at a jump of around 700 mAh. It’s only 14%, but that’s a considerable step up after years of stagnation. Both devices are also listed with 60W wired charging.

But, in a world where silicon-carbon batteries are pushing Android flagships upwards of 6,000, 7,000, and even bigger batteries. The Oppo Find X10, for example, is rumored to pack in an 8,000 mAh battery when it debuts later this month. 

What do you think? Did Samsung do enough? Sound off in the comments below.

title: OpenAI just upgraded ChatGPT Voice in three ways
snippet: Talking to ChatGPT is getting better in three ways starting today. OpenAI is rolling out a collection of improvements to how ChatGPT Voice mode works. more…
fullText:
Talking to ChatGPT is getting better in three ways starting today. OpenAI is rolling out a collection of improvements to how ChatGPT Voice mode works. 

GPT-6, ChatGPT Work, and plugins

First, ChatGPT Voice can now be powered by OpenAI’s three GPT-6 models. Astra, the most capable, has been out for a few weeks. Sol and Luna, the new medium and small intelligence models were upgraded to GPT-6 yesterday.

Next, OpenAI says that plugins now work with ChatGPT Voice. This includes integration like email, calendar, and Slack. This was a big disconnect for ChatGPT Voice users before, so it should be a highly welcome change.

Lastly, ChatGPT Voice now works with ChatGPT Work on the web and mobile. ChatGPT Work is OpenAI’s cloud-connected agentic system that works everywhere. It’s sort of like Codex on the desktop, but available in more places.

Back in July, OpenAI brought modern voice control to the ChatGPT desktop app. It’s great to see this focus on voice continue with today’s ChatGPT Voice-focused update.

title: AT&T seemingly has no plans to support Apple’s new iPhone Handoff feature
snippet: Apple last week launched a new iPhone Handoff feature, which lets you use a single phone number across two iPhones. The number intelligently moves between each iPhone based on whichever one you pick up. iPhone Handoff requires support from cellular carriers, and it sounds like AT&T isn’t interested in adopting the feature. more…
fullText:
Apple last week launched a new iPhone Handoff feature, which lets you use a single phone number across two iPhones. The number intelligently moves between each iPhone based on whichever one you pick up.

iPhone Handoff requires support from cellular carriers, and it sounds like AT&T isn’t interested in adopting the feature.

Will AT&T support iPhone Handoff? 

As reported by CNET, AT&T seemingly has no plans to support iPhone Handoff. According to the report:

“While we see that there could be potential in capabilities like iPhone Handoff,” the spokesperson replied, “our focus remains on delivering innovations that make life simpler and keep customers connected with confidence.” They then pointed to “existing eSIM activation and transfer options across compatible devices.”

This will be frustrating news for AT&T subscribers. The carrier’s emphasis on “existing eSIM activation and transfer options” seemingly indicates it doesn’t have a complete grasp on how iPhone Handoff works, and why it’s significantly more seamless than manually moving an eSIM back and forth between two iPhone models.

I’ve been using iPhone Handoff for the last week while testing the iPhone 18 Pro lineup, and it really does feel like magic. As Apple promised, my number instantly switches to whichever iPhone I pick up.

It is a bummer that T-Mobile is charging $5 per month for iPhone Handoff, though it’s not necessarily surprising. It’s still significantly cheaper than having a second cellular plan altogether.

As of right now, T-Mobile is the only carrier in the United States to support iPhone Handoff. Apple says that Verizon will add support by the end of the year, “with more carriers to follow.” Outside the United States, Telekom Germany is a launch partner for the feature. Apple says EE will add support by the end of the year.

title: Apple working on Whoop-style screenless fitness tracker, per report
snippet: Apple is developing a screenless health and fitness tracker to compete with Whoop, according to a new report from Bloomberg. The company is reportedly “developing prototypes,” but has yet to decide whether to ultimately release the product. more…
fullText:
Apple is developing a screenless health and fitness tracker to compete with Whoop, according to a new report from Bloomberg. The company is reportedly “developing prototypes,” but has yet to decide whether to ultimately release the product.

The prototypes being developed inside Apple reportedly have a “thin fabric band with a sensor-equipped computing module.” The project is currently in the “technology investigation” phase, and Bloomberg says the product won’t be released before 2028 — if Apple decides to release it at all.

The project is said to have support from top Apple executives, including Eddy Cue and Tim Cook. Cue took charge of Apple’s health team last October, following the departure of Jeff Williams.

Cue has pushed Apple’s health team to adopt features from the newer rivals, whose products offer simpler interfaces focused squarely on fitness and health tracking. The Apple Watch serves a broader range of purposes.

Products like Whoop and Oura Ring are popular among people who want to track their health and fitness without wearing a smartwatch. As Reuters reports, Oura is prepping for an IPO and recently revealed that it sold 3.6 million Oura Rings in the 12 months ending June 30. Revenue grew 74% to $1.21 billion for the nine months ending June 30.

Apple is still the dominant player in the smartwatch market specifically, though. The Apple Watch also offers a far wider array of features than health and fitness-focused wearables like Oura and Whoop.

Bloomberg also reiterates that next year will be a big year for the Apple Watch:

The company is also working on a major update to its smartwatch lineup for release as early as late 2027. This redesign would follow years of more incremental changes. Apple made its main watch thinner with the Series 10 two years ago, but the larger Ultra model has retained the same look since its debut four years ago.

title: Apple says software update to fix iPhone 18 Pro rebooting bug is coming next week
snippet: On Monday, we reported on an issue where iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max users were seeing their phone freeze and reboot following a failed Face ID attempt. To us, it appeared to be a software glitch rather than an inherent hardware fault. Apple has now confirmed to 9to5Mac that a software update to address this problem is in the works, and should be available early next week. more…
fullText:
On Monday, we reported on an issue where iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max users were seeing their phone freeze and reboot following a failed Face ID attempt. To us, it appeared to be a software glitch rather than an inherent hardware fault.

Apple has now confirmed to 9to5Mac that a software update to address this problem is in the works, and should be available early next week.

Although the bug did not seemingly affect all users, it was reasonably widespread based on social media and 9to5Mac reader reports. 

At the time, we reproduced the problem on an iPhone 18 Pro device by obscuring our face with our hand as we attempted a Face ID authentication to access the Passwords app. The phone simply stops responding to touch input, and hard reboots after a few seconds. You could then find a panic log in the iPhone Analytics section of the Settings app.

iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max feature a redesigned Face ID sensor system, where the Infrared camera has moved behind the under the screen near where the clock is rendered in the status bar, resulting in a 25% smaller visible Dynamic Island. 

As we reported earlier in the week, some customers had already attempted to resolve the rebooting problem by swapping their phone with a new device at Apple, thinking it was a hardware fault. To reiterate, this is not necessary with a software fix now confirmed to be on the way. 

On a somewhat related note, Apple also just released watchOS 27.0.1 to fix a random restart issue with Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4.

title: Clicks Communicator lands in December with 12GB RAM, two months of free data
snippet: Clicks — the company bringing physical keyboards back to mobile — is getting ready to ship its first-ever Android smartphone, and it’s shaping up to be a pretty interesting device. Ahead of its launch later this year, the company is upgrading a handful of the Clicks Communicator’s specs and announcing new accessories, protection coverage options, and eSIM plans. more…
fullText:
Clicks — the company bringing physical keyboards back to mobile — is getting ready to ship its first-ever Android smartphone, and it’s shaping up to be a pretty interesting device. Ahead of its launch later this year, the company is upgrading a handful of the Clicks Communicator’s specs and announcing new accessories, protection coverage options, and eSIM plans.

When the company announced the Clicks Communicator back at CES this year, it was primarily pitched as a secondary device meant to pair with your main smartphone. It seems like the team has heard from its potential customers that some might be satisfied with this being their main smartphone, which has prompted a handful of changes to improve the overall experience.

By far, the biggest upgrade is a move from 8GB to 12GB of RAM, something I’ll be calling a “reverse Pixel 11 Pro” situation. While other smartphone makers are doing whatever they can to reduce RAM — while increasing prices along the way — Clicks is adding additional memory to the device to better futureproof the phone. Its upgrade policy isn’t quite on par with Google or Samsung, but three promised OS upgrades and five years of security updates will, at the very least, pull your Communicator through to around 2032. Clicks has also moved its launch platform to Android 17 out of the box and bumped its battery capacity up to 4,350mAh. 

On the accessory side, Clicks and Dbrand are bringing the latter’s new MNML cases to the device, along with its Prism screen protector that includes a self-aligning tray — is there any other way? Clicks will also continue to offer its bumper Ring case for those looking for a more minimal approach to protection. Dbrand’s case and screen protector will run you $39 and $35, respectively, while the Ring bumper case is $49. Additional Charging Covers, allowing you to switch up your phone’s design, will also be available for $50 or $80, depending on material.

	

Finally, Clicks is launching both a protection plan and eSIM options for its users. Clicks Care is a $129 protection plan that delivers replacements or repairs for accidental damage over a two-year term with a $49 deductible; it’ll be available in the US and Canada. Clicks Mobile, meanwhile, is a new MVNO offering that brings voice and data to the Communicator via eSIM in the US and UK. Subscribers will receive two months of free service when activating their device at launch.

Clicks Communicator is set to ship in December, with reservation holders getting invites today to configure their final orders. September 30th — about two weeks away — is the last day to pre-order the device at its $499 launch price; starting October 1st, it moves to its base MSRP of $650. Anyone who scores the device as its cheaper starting price won’t be asked to pay more for its battery or RAM upgrades.

title: Apple and Qualcomm renew global patent licensing agreement
snippet: Qualcomm and Apple have renewed their global patent licensing agreement, extending a deal that was previously set to expire in 2027. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Qualcomm and Apple have renewed their global patent licensing agreement, extending a deal that was previously set to expire in 2027. Here are the details.

Renewed deal takes effect next year

To say that Apple and Qualcomm have had a rocky relationship would be an understatement.

Once major business partners, the companies became embroiled in a sprawling legal battle in 2017 over Qualcomm’s patent licensing practices and royalty payments.

In a nutshell, Apple sued Qualcomm in U.S. federal court in early 2017, challenging Qualcomm’s patent-licensing practices and seeking nearly $1 billion in royalty rebates that Apple said Qualcomm had improperly withheld.

The lawsuit came just three days after the FTC also sued Qualcomm, alleging anticompetitive licensing practices. The complaint specifically mentioned Qualcomm’s dealings with Apple, alleging that the company offered billions of dollars in conditional rebates in exchange for Apple exclusively using Qualcomm modem chips in new iPhones and iPads.

A few months later, Qualcomm countersued Apple, accusing the company of breaching agreements and interfering with its relationships with iPhone and iPad manufacturers.

The dispute ended in 2019, when Apple and Qualcomm agreed to drop all litigation against each other worldwide.

As part of the settlement, Apple made an undisclosed payment to Qualcomm that, among other things, resolved a dispute over royalty payments Apple had withheld during the legal battle. The companies also entered into a six-year global patent licensing agreement and a separate multiyear chipset supply deal.

That licensing agreement took effect on April 1, 2019, and included an option for Apple to extend it for another two years. Apple ultimately exercised that option, extending the agreement through March 2027.

Today, Qualcomm announced that the companies have renewed the agreement once again, with the new deal taking effect on April 1, 2027.

The full press release read:

Qualcomm Incorporated today announced the renewal of its global patent license agreement with Apple, effective April 1, 2027.

“We are pleased to extend the Apple license agreement,” said John Han, Executive Vice President and General Manager of Qualcomm Technology Licensing (QTL).

The company did not disclose how long the renewed agreement will remain in effect, while Apple has yet to comment on the renewal.

It is worth noting that today’s announcement is unrelated to Apple’s use of Qualcomm modems on iPhones, something that has been widely discussed recently, as Apple used a Qualcomm modem in the U.S. version of the iPhone 18 Pro Max while relying on its own C2 modem elsewhere.

Apple has not officially commented on what its modem plans will look like going forward, but the expectation has been that the company will eventually move away from Qualcomm modems altogether.
