title: Three weeks into the John Ternus era, Apple crosses its highest valuation ever
snippet: Apple shares briefly reached $345.34 moments after the market opened today, surpassing July’s intraday record of $344.57. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple shares briefly reached $345.34 moments after the market opened today, surpassing July’s intraday record of $344.57. Here are the details.

Apple stock reaches all-time-high

While Tim Cook appeared poised to hand over the reins to John Ternus with Apple’s valuation at an all-time high, the company’s last quarterly results spooked investors, sending the stock down roughly 10%.

Despite continued volatility, Apple gradually recovered some of those losses in the weeks that followed. On the day Cook passed the baton, shares closed at $316.85, giving the company a market capitalization of roughly $4.68 trillion.

Soon after Ternus took over, Apple shares fell as much as 3% in the run-up to the “Surprise and Shine” event. Historically, Apple’s stock has tended to react negatively to its September product events. This year, however, the response was overwhelmingly positive, both on Wall Street and among the general public.

Today, Apple shares gained roughly 1% to $345.34 after the market opened, briefly pushing the stock past its previous all-time high of $344.57. At the time of publication, Apple shares were trading at $341.80.

While it is still far too early to attribute the rally to Ternus alone, Apple shares have steadily climbed over the past three weeks since he took over as CEO, suggesting investors are responding positively to the leadership change and the company’s current roadmap.

fullText:
PITAKA’s iPhone 18 Pro cases bring new colors, updated materials, and three different approaches to protecting your next iPhone. Whether you prefer a barely-there shell or a case with reinforced corners, the new lineup builds on the company’s signature woven aramid fiber design with style.

The collection includes the Edge Case, Cairn Case, and Summa Case for iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. PITAKA also has an Edge option for Apple’s new foldable iPhone 18 Duo, with separate back shell and front frame options. 9to5Mac readers can also save 10% with promo code PITAKA10OFF now through October 9.

Edge Case keeps things light with comfort

If you like a slim case with a textured finish, the Edge Case delivers both from $59.99. Its woven aramid fiber shell focuses on lightness and fit, with a subtle grain that adds texture to the grip.

For this generation, PITAKA introduces Mammoth Resin. The company says it improves drop protection by 80% compared with the previous generation, following 14 months of development, more than 300 formula tests, and over 400 drop tests.

The Edge Case also includes PITAKA’s PitaTap Camera Control button. A capacitive sensor sits within less than 1mm of aramid fiber, integrating the control into the shell for a consistent look and feel. Meanwhile, a built-in Amber Magnetic Module supports MagSafe accessories.

PITAKA also adds a curved “P-angle” beneath the camera frame. This is purposefully designed to resist cracking when installing or removing the case. A bottom speaker cutout and chamfered side edge round out the updated design.

Enhance your iPhone 18 Pro | iPhone 18 Pro Max

Cairn Case adds reinforced corners

For a more rugged design, the $59.99 Cairn Case pairs aramid fiber with slip-resistant TPU. The woven back contrasts with a nice matte frame. This gives the case a textured appearance that carries through to its protective edges.

Cairn belongs to PITAKA’s Guard Series and features Bow-Arc Corner Buffer 2.0. Inspired by the geometry of heavy-duty outdoor gear, the design uses reinforced, flared corners to help absorb impact from drops.

Instead of the Edge Case’s integrated PitaTap design, Cairn uses a physical capacitive camera button. It covers the control area, avoiding the open cutout approach while keeping the Camera Control within reach.

The combination makes Cairn the lineup’s option for anyone who prefers pronounced corner protection and an outdoor-inspired look, with aramid fiber still central to the design.

Protect your iPhone 18 Pro | iPhone 18 Pro Max

Summa Case wraps the edges in aramid fiber

The $79.99 Summa Case takes a different approach to the Guard Series. It uses 3D thermoforming to extend aramid fiber all the way to the shell’s edge. This creates a continuous woven appearance.

PITAKA pairs that wraparound construction with its Orca Resin. The company describes this as a durable material designed to balance slimness and protection. Summa also includes a physical capacitive Camera Control and a lanyard hole.

The woven look is what defines PITAKA, and Summa carries that detail beyond the back panel. Its full-wrap construction extends the material across the case’s overall appearance.

title: TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026: Everything you need to know
snippet: TechCrunch Founder Summit is a full-day gathering in Boston on November 4 where founders across all stages connect with top VCs and experienced entrepreneurs to gain tactical insights on building and scaling their companies.
fullText:
TechCrunch Founder Summit is a full-day gathering in Boston on November 4 where founders across all stages connect with top VCs and experienced entrepreneurs to gain tactical insights on building and scaling their companies. It’s the latest in our long line of founder-centric events, which are smaller and more hands-on than Disrupt.

If an extensive lineup of speakers from Anthropic, Nvidia, OpenAI, and Benchmark is your thing, Disrupt tickets are still available here. But for the founder looking to really get in the weeds during a one-day crash course, Founder Summit is the ideal place to get a head start on your 2027 plans. 

Before you dig in on the event details, you can get info on all of our tickets, which are available for a $200 discount for investors and founders, right here.

Who is TechCrunch Founder Summit for? 

All founders end up wrestling with the extensive, complicated mechanics of building a company from the ground up. There’s fundraising, hiring, legal, marketing, PR, and leadership, as well as the investors needing the means to vet, invest in, and develop founders as they build out their skills.

Founder Summit is the best way to cover all of the challenging questions with community members who have been there, and lived to tell the tale, through constructive failure and massive success.

When and where is TechCrunch Founder Summit? 

The event takes place on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, at the SoWa Power Station in Boston. It’s accessible via public transportation and a short walk from the Back Bay and Tufts Medical Center stops on the Orange Line, or the Broadway stop on the Red Line.

Image Credits:TechCrunch / Getty Images

What’s on the TechCrunch Founder Summit agenda? 

To deliver on that promise of equipping founders for success, this year’s agenda and speakers lean hard into fundraising, AI-native building, and leadership. Sessions include:

The New Rules of Raising Capital: Brian Devaney, partner at Underscore, breaking down what investors look for now and where founders lose leverage without realizing it. 

The CEO Job Never Gets Easier: HubSpot co-founder and Sequoia partner Brian Halligan on how the CEO role changes at each stage of growth. 

Built for AI From Day One: 7AI co-founder and CEO Lior Div on what changes when AI is the foundation of a company rather than a bolt-on feature. 

Not Every Dollar Is Equal: Cogent Security co-founder and CEO Vineet Edupuganti on evaluating investors and cap-table trade-offs beyond valuation. 

How to Spot the ‘King of the Hill’ Company: TDK Ventures investment director Tina Tosukhowong unpacking a framework for evaluating startups on economics, scalability, and timing. 

Your Company Is Who You Hire: NEA partner Melissa Taunton on early hiring decisions that shape a startup’s culture and execution. 

The Boston Founder Playbook: HqO co-founder and CEO Chase Garbarino on building a category-defining company outside Silicon Valley, having raised $200 million and scaled to 30+ countries.   

Finding Product Market Fit Before You Scale: Bessemer Venture Partners‘ Kent Bennett on validating demand and avoiding scaling before the fundamentals are in place.

Didn’t this event have a different name? 

Yes. Founder Summit was formerly known as Early Stage and All Stage. This year, we have the same mission, but with a new name. Keep that in mind if you want to do any more research before attending.

Is TechCrunch Founder Summit just panels, or is there more to it? 

Founder Summit is far from a series of panels, though the agenda does provide a ton of valuable insights for founders and investors. In addition to all of those sessions, we also have our breakout sessions, where even more intimate panels discuss vital topics for the community to dive deeper into.

There’s also networking available via the Braindate app to help connect investors with founders, or facilitate founders with similar challenges to bring their expertise together to reach shared solutions. Or that time is the perfect opportunity for students to build out their nascent network.

Then there’s Founder Summit week, taking place November 1-7. That’s when all of our Side Events are held, expanding the opportunities for you to gather with the community. And if you’re especially eager to take part, you can apply to host your own Side Event right here.

Image Credits:Halo Creative

How much does a ticket cost, and how can I get the best price? 

Pricing moves in phases, with our next increase happening after October 16. Our current pricing tiers are Investor for $399, Founder for $199, and students for $149. If you buy a second ticket for a co-founder or co-worker, you’ll also get 50% off their admission. And bundles for groups for four or more offer additional discounts.

Is there a free way to attend? 

Yes! We’re looking for volunteers to help staff the event, and those individuals will get a behind-the-scenes look at how the event comes together on top of their free access to programming beyond their shift. Learn more about our program, which closes to new applicants October 19, right here.

Where can I register and learn more? 

You can get the full rundown of the event, with everything from up-to-date speaker information, the full agenda, logistics, and more right here. Ticket information across all three tiers is available here. And remember, our current discounts end October 16 — act now before they expire.

title: Here’s what’s really going on with GM’s CarPlay strategy (or lack thereof)
snippet: Despite headlines to the contrary, GM isn’t changing its position on CarPlay and Android Auto support. The automaker is not bringing phone projection support back to any cars from which it has already been removed. Here’s what’s really happening. more…
fullText:
Despite headlines to the contrary, GM isn’t changing its position on CarPlay and Android Auto support. The automaker is not bringing phone projection support back to any cars from which it has already been removed. Here’s what’s really happening. 

No, GM isn’t walking back its decision to ditch CarPlay

The confusion started when GM announced a new software experience for its Chevy Silverado and GMC Sierra trucks last week. The company touted a new picture-in-picture phone mirroring system in which CarPlay and Android Auto would coexist alongside GM’s native infotainment system.

Some sources interpreted this news as GM backtracking on its plan to ditch CarPlay, which it first announced in 2023. Unfortunately, that is not the case. GM’s original announcement was about dropping CarPlay support from its future EVs. It has followed through on that plan, except for the Cadillac Lyriq EV.

GM has not removed CarPlay or Android Auto from any of its gas-powered cars. Therefore, the new phone projection system in the Chevy Silverado and GMC Sierra trucks is not the automaker caving to the pressure and bringing CarPlay support back to its EVs.

A GM spokesperson confirmed this to Joanna Stern, who posted the following on X today:

Correction: GM has confirmed it is NOT rolling phone projection to GM EVs. Instead this announcement is specific to JUST their new gas powered light-duty pickups, which have always supported Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

The confusion is reasonable. GM CEO Mary Barra said in an interview that the automaker would remove CarPlay and Android Auto from gas cars at some point. The company quickly clarified, however, that gas cars would continue to offer phone projection “for the foreseeable future.”

All that’s to say, nothing has changed. GM isn’t bringing CarPlay back to its EVs. The company’s strategy has not changed. Perhaps we can interpret GM’s picture-in-picture solution for select gas cars as a sign that it’s aware the decision to ditch CarPlay is unpopular. I think that’s too favorable an interpretation, though.

title: Chrome now saves scroll position, filled forms when sending tabs between devices
snippet: Google today announced a trio of new study-focused Chrome features, with the most notable being how the browser will now save scroll position when you send tabs between devices. more…
fullText:
Google today announced a trio of new study-focused Chrome features, with the most notable being how the browser will now save scroll position when you send tabs between devices.

When you send a page from mobile to laptop (or vice versa), Chrome will now save the “exact state of your tab when you send it over.” This includes the scroll position and partially filled-in forms: “if you’re halfway through a 50-page paper on behavioral economics, you can send it to your phone and pick up exactly where you left during your commute.”

On desktop, you can do this from the three-dot overflow menu > Cast, Save, and Share > Send to Your Device. The shortcut can also be added to your toolbar from Customize Chrome (on the New Tab Page) > Toolbar. In Chrome for Android, open Chrome’s share menu for the carousel of options.

Gemini in Chrome now lets you ask questions about videos, podcasts, recordings, and other types of media that aren’t on YouTube. Google touts how the side panel can now “identify key takeaways, find specific information, or clarify confusing moments for almost any audio or video file once you’ve played it through.”

	

Meanwhile, Gemini in Chrome can now generate interactive quizzes with the content of your current tab. This can include Google Docs, YouTube videos, research papers, and more. The tool will “highlight core concepts and help you check your understanding.” Quizzes are coming to English in the US and India on desktop and will come to more regions and mobile in the “coming months.”

Google is highlighting other existing tools like vertical or horizontal tabs, Split View, and tab groups. There’s also immersive reading mode and read aloud.

title: Apple didn’t give up on stylus support for iPhone Duo; Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold should take notes
snippet: Apple’s iPhone Duo may not have reinvented the Android foldable, but it certainly did put a polish on a number of things. Inlcuded in that list is stylus support on the iPhone Duo, something that was more complicated behind-the-scenes than it initially sounded like, and an effort that Samsung should probably take note of. more…
fullText:
Apple’s iPhone Duo may not have reinvented the Android foldable, but it certainly did put a polish on a number of things. Inlcuded in that list is stylus support on the iPhone Duo, something that was more complicated behind-the-scenes than it initially sounded like, and an effort that Samsung should probably take note of.

Rewinding, Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold series first added stylus support back in 2022 on the Galaxy Z Fold 3. Samsung made a special version of the S Pen stylus for foldables that didn’t require a battery, but also didn’t stow away inside of the foldable. Still, it was fully supported and a welcome tool, especially as the Galaxy Note series was dying off. But with last year’s Galaxy Z Fold 7, Samsung ditched support for the S Pen in order to make the foldable much thinner.

S Pen support on Galaxy Z Fold 4 and Fold 5

But, of course, Samsung is likely rethinking that decision now that Apple has introduced the iPhone Duo with stylus support.

Apple touts that the iPhone Duo will support the USB-C version of the Apple Pencil that’s otherwise made for iPads. It sounds simple enough, but there’s more to the story. Bloomberg reports that Apple originally wanted to make a dedicated version of Apple Pencil for the iPhone Duo, a version that would have been shorter and able to magnetically hold itself on the Duo’s hinge. 

	

That stylus wasn’t announced as, apparently, Apple ran into “technical problems ahead of mass production” a few months before the Duo was announced, leading to the pivot over to iPad versions of the stylus. The report further notes that Apple’s software update to enable this isn’t “as simple as hitting a button” and that it won’t arrive until “fairly late in 2026.” 

Still, that’s more than Samsung is bringing to the table at this point. Both the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Fold 8 Ultra lack any support for a stylus, despite rumors of Samsung exploring other ways of offering a stylus on its foldables. The reason the traditional S Pen doesn’t work in these thin form factors is that it requires a physical layer in the display assembly and, as such, adds to the thickness and weight – two pillars that Samsung is hyper-focused on improving with each generation. 

Samsung’s Android competition has embraced stylus support, so between that and Apple’s adoption (mostly the latter, obviously), it’s all the more likely Galaxy Z Fold 9 will bring stylus support page in one form or another. Samsung has left the door open, too.

title: Pixel VIPs 2.0 redesign starts rolling out with fullscreen look
snippet: Following last week’s Feature Drop, Pixel VIPs 2.0 is beginning to roll out, and it brings more changes than just the widget redesign. more…
fullText:
Following last week’s Feature Drop, Pixel VIPs 2.0 is beginning to roll out, and it brings more changes than just the widget redesign.

With version 2.0, tapping on a contact in the widget no longer slides up a bottom sheet over your homescreen. Instead, it now opens a fullscreen layout, which was previously accessible by swiping up. The previous design was better for one-handed use as the call and message shortcuts were closer to the bottom of the screen.

Other changes to this page include a pencil icon in the top-right corner that lets you quickly edit in Google Contacts, while the call, message, video, and contact buttons now use outline-style icons.

Old vs. new

	

Google has moved the “Local updates” card to the top spot over “Last connection,” while “Notes” is now the last section as Pixel VIPs has removed the media and place recommendations.

Meanwhile, the big update today is a new pill-shaped switcher that shows all your VIPs. This allows for quick switching without having to go back to the homescreen.

The actual widget redesign is not yet live after updating to Pixel VIPs 2.0. However, there is a preview of the new layout with “space for quick actions” that lets you call and message directly from the widget.

Pixel VIPs 2.0 is widely rolled out via the Play Store.

title: Googlebook OS hands-on: It’s Android, stupid
snippet: An overwhelming sense of familiarity struck me the first time I used a Googlebook. That was immediately followed by a realization that this is just Android, and I think that feeling of similarity will go a long way in justifying and ultimately selling Googlebooks. more…
fullText:
An overwhelming sense of familiarity struck me the first time I used a Googlebook. That was immediately followed by a realization that this is just Android, and I think that feeling of similarity will go a long way in justifying and ultimately selling Googlebooks.

Going into this event, I was not particularly asking for a desktop operating system that felt like my Pixel phone. In fact, having used Chromebooks for many years (my first unit was the 2013 Acer C720), I thought Googlebook OS would not feel too different from ChromeOS. The desktop and app dock look the same, but the changes made by building on top of Android make all the difference.

That shared design and user experience allowed me to immediately start using Googlebook OS like a near-expert. Quick Settings and Notifications were obviously in the top-right corner, matching Android’s conventions. It’s a small change compared to ChromeOS, but it felt natural the first time I used it. I knew immediately to move the cursor to that top corner instead of the usual bottom corner on Chromebooks.

I also knew I could add and edit widgets, a long-requested feature ChromeOS lacks, by long-pressing on the desktop, while seeing the same ones from my phone homescreen evoked an almost nostalgia-like feeling.

	

The Settings app is identical to that on Pixel phones, while I was very happy to find Pixel Weather (and its widgets) along with the excellent Recorder pre-installed. Meanwhile, the app drawer is basically the Pixel Launcher. Compared to ChromeOS, you can put apps, widgets, and files/folders on the desktop for an infinite boost to productivity.

The best of the web 

Given how much Googlebook OS felt like using my Pixel phone, it was surprising to see that launching Gmail and Google Calendar opened the web versions rather than the Android apps. Talking with Google, I later learned that these were Trusted Web Activities (TWAs) instead of PWAs. Distributed from the Play Store, their main advantage is how this web wrapper-esque format allows for homescreen widgets.  

Zooming out, what shocked me was how much Googlebook OS leverages web apps, a move that strongly affirms the ChromeOS lineage. Going in, I assumed there would be a resurgence in desktop-class Android apps. 

However, I am told this was an intentional choice. Google’s viewpoint is ultimately to let app developers decide what the best strategy is for their application, and I think that’s fair. Google offered me the example of how it approached the Gmail and Workspace teams about whether they wanted to offer Googlebook adopters the web version or the Android app. They chose the former and ideally did not want to offer the Android app as an available Play Store download.

However, I do think this is partially a missed opportunity. Giving third-party developers a choice does reduce the barrier to entry for a new OS, but I strongly think Google internally should have enforced a strict first-party mandate to create desktop-class applications. 

Meanwhile, as I complained about in my Pixel Tablet review three years ago, it’s unbelievable that Google Messages is still using the same web-based version rather than anything more native. 

The Chrome browser on Googlebooks feels great and offers a full-featured experience from extensions to the new vertical tab list.

For all Android, always

That said, other experiences are clearly Android-powered. This includes the Google app and Gemini. When you invoke the Magic Pointer overlay, prompt responses appear in the Android Gemini app.

More broadly, Google sees this Android-based OS as an opportunity to leverage the existing Gemini and AI work done for phones as a starting point for the desktop. This is compared to having to rebuild everything from scratch for ChromeOS.

The on-device AI model is Gemini Nano, and that’s used to power AI descriptions of your screenshots that unlock search, as well as Magic Pointer, Rambler, and Create My Widget via a hybrid intelligence architecture.

I have to use the much-derided Magic Pointer a bit more to determine whether it’s some groundbreaking UX paradigm, but I do credit it for being very easy to enable. You will not forget that this feature exists on Googlebooks, and I think that could be valuable.

Rambler is the other major Gemini Intelligence feature, and you launch it from a Quick Insert key that’s in place of Caps Lock. Pressing the new Quick Insert key launches a rather convenient floating window that provides quick access to emoji, recent screenshots, and the Gboard clipboard, with Rambler in the bottom-right corner. This is a rather smart carryover from ChromeOS, now accessible with a single key press rather than a three-key combo.

Create My Widget is the other major tentpole. This is the introduction of generative UI to Android, and I think the ramifications for the future are tremendous. Right now, you get to make widgets that pull from live data sources, like Search. Googlebooks will definitely have to guide people on how to use this capability, but I think this could be a powerful selling point.

Google is adopting the successful Android OEM model for Googlebooks. However, they’ve fortunately drawn a line on how updates will work. Google is responsible for rolling out Googlebook OS updates, not OEMs, carrying over one of the strongest elements of ChromeOS. Partners will be able to specify preloaded apps, but they can’t do any heavy customization like altering what the status bar icons look like. The experience of using a Googlebook will be universal across partners. 

	

Google will be releasing major Googlebook OS updates on a quarterly basis to match the Android Quarterly Platform Release (QPR) model, but security updates can come at any time in between. 

Closing

Google spent a long time developing Googlebooks, and it shows. The specific example that really surprised me is that Google built an Antigravity app with native UI for Android. Going in, I thought they would just offer the Linux version, but this Antigravity for Android is distributed via the Play Store and interacts with the Linux terminal environment on Googlebook OS.

Frankly, Google fumbled its initial unveiling of Googlebooks in May. It was officially intended only as a preview, but the decision to highlight only a handful of features, including Magic Pointer, ended up being a great disservice. Googlebook OS is so much more than that, and the company should have led with the Android nature right off the bat.

Again, we actually have to see if it works in our daily workflows, but my initial impression is that Android gives Googlebooks a very solid foundation.

title: Here’s everything new for Apple Calendar in iOS 27
snippet: iOS 27 is packed with new features for Apple Wallet, Messages, Notes, and other system apps—including Calendar. Here’s everything new for Apple’s Calendar app in iOS 27. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 is packed with new features for Apple Wallet, Messages, Notes, and other system apps—including Calendar. Here’s everything new for Apple’s Calendar app in iOS 27.

Natural language input for events and reminders

Calendar adds a feature in iOS 27 that’s been on my wishlist for years: natural language input.

Apple calls this ‘Smart Event Details,’ and it’s powered by Apple Intelligence. Here’s how it’s described:

Type events in your own words. Apple Intelligence fills in the title, time, location, and invitees as you go.

This works for both events and reminders. You can type in natural language when creating or editing an event, and watch the event details automatically fill in based on what you type.

If you prefer the manual approach, you can toggle this off in Settings, but I’ve been very happy to have it.

Design updates

Apple has updated Calendar’s design in iOS 27 in two main places:

Event details view

Event creation and editing

When you tap an event, it now pops up in a card overlay with a fresh design. Event options have been reorganized and given icons to make them visually pop.

And for event creation and editing, iOS 27 has an updated look too. Like with event details, Apple has reorganized the various options and added icons for each category.

Show as Busy/Free option for iCloud calendars

With modern digital calendars, the ability to mark yourself as busy or free related to a given event is a pretty standard feature. But until iOS 27, that option never existed for iCloud calendars.

If you use a Google calendar inside Apple’s app, you’ll see the event option to show yourself as busy or free. But for iCloud calendars, that’s long been missing.

iOS 27 finally remedies the oversight, offering a free/busy option for iCloud events like you would get for events from Google and other third-party calendar providers.

iOS 27 lets you make Home Screen and Today widgets bigger than ever thanks to a new extra-large size. And Calendar supports two extra-large widgets.

You can set up ’List’ and ‘Up Next’ widgets in the extra-large size. Each is great for showing more events and reminders than ever, so if you have a packed calendar, the new widgets could prove useful.

Extra-large widgets take up a lot of screen real estate, but they should prove especially handy on the iPhone Duo’s extra-large display.

Siri AI upgrades

It’s worth mentioning that Siri AI comes with plenty of upgrades relevant to the Calendar app.

Siri gains onscreen awareness, understands your personal context, and is overall more intelligent and capable than ever before. That means it’s a much better tool for managing your calendar. In my use of iOS 27, I’ve found myself relying much more on Siri for handling events and reminders.

There’s also a new visual intelligence button in the event creation screen that lets you scan an event flyer with the new Siri mode in the Camera app. Siri then creates a new event with the details.

title: Former Apple retail chief’s new ‘Shop Different’ book now available
snippet: Ron Johnson, Apple’s former senior vice president of retail operations, is out with a new book today called ‘Shop Different: How Retail Revealed Apple’s Genius.’ In the book, Johnson tells the story of working alongside Steve Jobs to craft Apple’s retail strategy. more…
fullText:
Ron Johnson, Apple’s former senior vice president of retail operations, is out with a new book today called ‘Shop Different: How Retail Revealed Apple’s Genius.’

In the book, Johnson tells the story of working alongside Steve Jobs to craft Apple’s retail strategy.

‘Shop Different,’ written with Zander Nethercutt, isn’t a “traditional business book,” but rather an “insider account of one of the most important retail successes of our time.”

Here’s the description:

When Steve Jobs hired Ron Johnson to create the Apple Store in 2000, con­ventional wisdom said that the inter­net would put stores out of business. By the time he left Apple in 2011, Johnson and his team had created the most respected and profitable retail stores in the world. And even then, skeptics were still predicting the death of physical retail.

In Shop Different, Johnson reveals how it happened: how he earned Jobs’s trust, how they developed a vision for a store that would win not by selling but by serving, and how he convinced Jobs that the store’s service philosophy should be rooted in some­thing as intangible as love. Johnson then gives readers a new look at Apple’s ascent to the most valuable company in the world; offers an inspiring vision for a future in which retailers win on connection, service, and experience; and shares an honest look at what leads to success—and what can follow.

Johnson joined 9to5Mac’s Overtime podcast last week to discuss ‘Shop Different’ and the origins of the Apple Store. Jeff and Fernando did an excellent job interviewing Johnson, and you can watch it on YouTube, or listen via Apple Podcasts and other platforms.

‘Shop Different: How Retail Revealed Apple’s Genius’ can be ordered on Amazon today. You can also order it and support local bookstores via Bookshop.org. My copy arrives today and I’m looking forward to diving in.

title: Gemini app for macOS adding send and read iMessage integration
snippet: Google’s latest update to the Gemini app for macOS readies local iMessage integration. This follows the app coming to Windows last week. more…
fullText:
Google’s latest update to the Gemini app for macOS readies local iMessage integration. This follows the app coming to Windows last week.

Gemini’s latest Connected App on the Mac is @messages to “Read, search, and send messages in Apple Messages.” Specifically, the integration can:

Send messages to contacts or phone numbers

Read recent conversations, unread messages, and search message history

This will aid context by being able to look up information from conversations. Example prompts include:

Send a message to John: “Running 5 minutes late!”

Show my recent messages from Sarah

Search Messages for dinner reservations

 In terms of limitations, Gemini cannot:

	

Manage group participant membership or change group chat photos

Schedule messages for future delivery or edit sent messages

Send file, photo, or media attachments (plain text messages only)

Send tapback reactions (love, like, dislike, laugh, emphasize, question)

Generate photos or images within automated task workflows

This integration appears in Settings > Connected Apps at the very bottom after updating to version 1.116.5.889 of Gemini for macOS. However, as of this afternoon, a server-side component appears to be missing, with @messages not yet recognized in the prompt box.

Recent updates to Gemini for macOS introduced a File Providers extension that shows “Add to Gemini” when you right-click on a file in Finder. This immediately adds the photo or document to the prompt box. It can be enabled in Settings > Extensions. Google also added Images, Videos, and Daily Brief to the side panel.

title: Gmail adds ‘Copy code’ shortcut for 2FA on Android & iOS
snippet: After rolling out Live search and chat earlier this month, Gmail now has a useful “Copy code” button for 2FA on Android and iOS. more…
fullText:
After rolling out Live search and chat earlier this month, Gmail now has a useful “Copy code” button for 2FA on Android and iOS.

Instead of having to open an email to select and copy the two-factor authentication code, Gmail now shows a shortcut directly in your inbox. The pill-shaped “Copy code 000000” button appears below the subject line, like the previews for images, documents, and other attachments.

Tapping the button simply adds the code to your clipboard for a quick paste in the designated app. 

We’ve seen it work for store and banking emails in our brief testing today. It’s a nice quality-of-life addition.

	

The Copy code button is appearing in Gmail for Android (version 2026.09.07.x) and iOS (6.0.260907), but not on the web. This shortcut would also be useful in email notifications on Android.

title: Rare ‘Antennagate’ press conference Q&A video surfaces online
snippet: The Q&A session of one of Apple’s most notable events in the last 20 years has surfaced online, and you should watch it before it vanishes. Watch it below. more…
fullText:
The Q&A session of one of Apple’s most notable events in the last 20 years has surfaced online, and you should watch it before it vanishes. Watch it below.

Watch it before Apple pulls it

Even if you didn’t follow Apple closely back in 2010, you have probably heard about Antennagate and the last-minute press conference that pulled Steve Jobs from a family vacation in Hawaii.

If you’re just joining us, here’s what happened: Soon after Apple released the iPhone 4, users noticed that the cell signal would drop significantly depending on how they held the device.

The commotion around this was big enough that Apple scheduled an emergency event just weeks after the iPhone 4 hit the shelves.

In it, Jobs explained that the signal drop wasn’t exclusive to the iPhone 4, but that users would have the choice to either get a free case to prevent their hands from making direct contact with the antenna, or return the phone for a full refund.

After the event, Jobs was joined by then-COO Tim Cook and Bob Mansfield, Apple’s senior vice president of Mac Hardware Engineering, for a Q&A with the press.

Since then, there have been multiple accounts of what was said during the Q&A, including John Gruber’s recollections from asking the question that prompted Jobs, Cook, and Mansfield to pull their caseless iPhones out of their pockets, resulting in one of the more memorable photos from that era. However, the actual video of the session had never surfaced. Until now.

Earlier this week, YouTube channel Sir Mix-A-Lot Rare Music (no apparent relation to the actual Sir Mix-A-Lot) published the entire 47-minute Q&A session, which you can watch below:

There is no information on how the channel obtained the video or whether Apple plans to file a copyright takedown request. But now that the footage is out there, copies could easily resurface elsewhere even if the original upload disappears.

The mere fact that the video is still up is a good sign. That said, if you want to see this little piece of Apple history for yourself, you might want to watch it sooner rather than later.

Did you already follow Apple back in the Antennagate days? Let us know in the comments.

title: YouTube announces Custom Feeds, GIF comments, and ’Your podcast lineup’
snippet: At Made on YouTube 2026 today, YouTube announced a slew of new features. We’ve highlighted the capabilities that will impact the viewer experience over the coming months. more…
fullText:
At Made on YouTube 2026 today, YouTube announced a slew of new features. We’ve highlighted the capabilities that will impact the viewer experience over the coming months.

YouTube app

Custom Feeds will let you conversationally create a dedicated tab from the Homepage for “specific moods, routines, or your latest interests.” Multiple feeds can be created, with examples including “evening wind down with long documentaries” or “new DIY creators.” This feature is coming to US users on web, mobile, and TVs “soon.”

Ask YouTube is getting shopping features that let you “receive organized video recommendations, such as a comparison table that includes product attributes and categories based on your preferences.”

Once you click on a video that interests you most, you can continue asking more questions about the product directly on the video’s watch page.

This fall, YouTube comments will support GIFs. The mobile comment box will let you search a library of GIFs with this type of commenting available on videos and Shorts.

	

The in-app direct messaging feature is adding support for group chats. This is coming this fall in the US, UK, Singapore, Brazil, and some European countries.

YouTube Music + Podcasts

YouTube Music is getting a “personalized AI-audio guide” called Your podcast lineup. You get a “weekly spoken preview of recommended shows” that will dive into why you’ll like them. It then proceeds to suggested episodes, with this touted as being a “completely eyes-optional and hands-free” experience.

Meanwhile, the Ask Music chat found in the Home tab is getting new features that let you “customize your queue or dive deeper into artist lore.”

Both updates are “coming soon to YouTube Music and Premium subscribers worldwide.”

YouTube will stream Coachella through 2030. The 2027 edition will mark “15 years of bringing the desert festival experience to fans worldwide.”

YouTube Shorts 

YouTube is introducing a Shorts series feature that lets Creators organize their Shorts into seasons and episodes for a more structured and episodic experience. This is rolling out starting today. 

In a related development, the Shorts feed will start to recommend posts. Google shared that over 300 million users engage with Posts on YouTube every day. These text posts will also be coming to TVs in the “coming months.”

For YouTube Creators 

YouTube is piloting a Live auto-dubbing feature in early 2027 that “automatically translates your speech in real time” to let viewers “listen along in their preferred language as you speak.”

YouTube is testing “opt-in AI-powered comment moderation.” It will learn your “unique moderation style and needs over time.”
